smell_validity.evidence: ToastManager absorbs eight unrelated clusters—module-global ref registry, options resolution, React lifecycle, timers, keyboard listeners, layout/animation math, gesture dispatch, renderer lookup—while the demoted cohesive owners remain visible as one-line forwarding shims. Four per-render session types show the class holding foreign per-hook state; the accretion, lost cohesion, and its cost are unmistakable without the label.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Every concern—keyboard fixes, animation tweaks, timer changes, new renderers—now edits one ~750-line file while ten modules hollow into forwarders. Per-render session rebinding is a standing stale-capture hazard, and the static/instance split invites ownership mistakes. Repair restores the library's entire responsibility and dependency architecture, far beyond tidier local edits.

development_plausibility.evidence: Moved code is verbatim with original comments, TODOs, issue links, types, and export signatures; each absorption step mirrors real centralization rationales, so it sits naturally beside surrounding code. But absorbing even one-line helpers (array inversion, layout getters) and the uniform four-session bind-per-render pattern show task-shaped regularity a real maintainer would rarely extend to trivial utilities.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: Names the smell, enumerates each responsibility cluster and thinned module, pins the full export inventory and precise semantics (callback order, freshness, unknown-type throw, per-instance isolation), and bans cosmetic re-splits, pass-through layers, leftover trampolines, and test/build edits while leaving owner form free. A model contract that decisively prevents wrong direction, incomplete cleanup, and irrelevant redesign.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Eight clusters demand distinct code-supported decisions: module-global registry identity, per-mount timer cleanup and cancel-on-unmount, effect-gated iOS listeners, per-render closure freshness in the lifecycle, memoized interpolation dependencies, responder construction cadence, and throw-on-unknown renderer lookup. No single decision rule repeats across the counted purposes.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt's cluster list plus its public-API inventory already names every affected module, and the manager is the only such class under src/. One direct-caller/imports search confirms no hidden consumers; no cross-component data-flow combination is needed to classify any location or to spot excluded cohesive modules.

repair_coordination.evidence: Registry producer/consumer identity, timer-cancel-on-hide, per-mount listener lifetime, and per-render session freshness must hold across modules. A concrete partial repair—moving binding into a memo or effect—passes ordinary show/auto-hide flows but fails across stages: after an options change, stale sessions invoke the old onHide or visibilityTime silently.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: A uniform delegation-collapse repairs only pure static helpers (utils shims, layout and gesture math, renderer lookup, geometry exports)—under 40% of locations. Stateful clusters—lifecycle, timers, keyboard, gesture dispatch, swipe visuals, animation driving—lack forwarding shims and each needs separate freshness, cleanup, memoization, and ordering decisions; the class dissolves only after all leave.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Bind-once or memoized-session repairs compile and pass ordinary show/auto-hide flows, failing only in special state: stale callbacks on the second options update, two mounted toasts sharing one owner, or the unknown-type throw. Multiple hidden failure paths exist, but no test code appears in evidence, so score-4 unchecked-path conditions cannot be established.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
